'''Martin James Wainwright''' (born 1973)<!-- Middle name and birth year sourced from meta data of the library entry for his thesis (see following reference), where it lists "Wainwright, Martin J. (Martin James), 1973–" as the author. His middle name also listed at the Mathematics Genealogy Project. --><ref name="PhDthesis">{{cite thesis |last=Wainwright |first=Martin J. |date=2002 |title=Stochastic processes on graphs with cycles: geometric and variational approaches |url=https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/8371 |degree=Ph.D. |chapter= |publisher=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science |hdl=1721.1/8371 |access-date=October 3, 2024}}</ref> is a statistician and the Cecil H. Green Professor in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and Mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT), a position he has held since July 2022. At MIT, Wainwright is also affiliated with the [[MIT Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems|Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems]], where he is a principal investigator, and a member of the Statistics and Data Science Center.<ref name="LIDS2022joins">{{cite web |title=Martin Wainwright joins MIT faculty and LIDS |url=https://lids.mit.edu/news-and-events/news/martin-wainwright-joins-mit-faculty-and-lids |website=[[MIT Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems]] |publisher=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |date=July 1, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Martin Wainwright |url=https://stat.mit.edu/people/martin-wainwright/ |website=MIT Statistics + Data Science Center |publisher=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221129001934/https://stat.mit.edu/people/martin-wainwright/ |archive-date=November 29, 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Before joining MIT in 2022, Wainwright was part of the faculty at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he held the Howard Friesen Chair at the time of his departure.<ref name="LIDS2022joins" />

==Education and career==
Wainwright earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from the [[University of Waterloo]] in 1994<ref name="COPSSWaterloo">{{cite web |title=COPSS Award for alumnus Martin Wainwright |url=https://uwaterloo.ca/math/news/copss-award-alumnus-martin-wainwright |publisher=[[University of Waterloo]] |access-date=October 3, 2024 |date=October 17, 2014 |archive-date=September 6, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906202530/https://uwaterloo.ca/math/news/copss-award-alumnus-martin-wainwright |url-status=live }}</ref> and a master's degree in [[vision science]] from [[Harvard University]] in 1998.<ref name="IEEEBiography2003">{{cite journal |title=Contributors |journal=[[IEEE Transactions on Information Theory]] |date=May 2003 |volume=49 |issue=5 |page=1381 |doi=10.1109/TIT.2003.810621 |quote=Martin J. Wainwright received the B.S. degree in mathematics from the University of Waterloo, Waterloo, ON, Canada, in 1994, the M.S. degree in vision science from Harvard University, Cambridge, MA, in 1998, and the Ph.D. degree in electrical engineering and computer science from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Cambridge, in 2002.}}</ref><ref name="LIDS2011data">{{cite magazine |last1=Wanucha |first1=Genevieve |title=Data Deluge |url=https://lidsmag.lids.mit.edu/2011/data_deluge.html |magazine=LIDS/ALL |publisher=[[MIT Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems]] |access-date=October 3, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221008124108/https://lidsmag.lids.mit.edu/2011/data_deluge.html |archive-date=October 8, 2022 |date=2011 |quote=Martin works as a professor ... at UC Berkeley. These days, he's spending his sabbatical here at LIDS. It's not far from home, actually, as Martin earned his PhD here in 2002. ... After receiving his undergraduate degree in mathematics, he [Wainwright] earned a Masters in neuroscience from Harvard. |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Alumni – Graduate Students |url=https://visionlab.harvard.edu/members.alumni.php?memberID=graduate |website=Harvard Vision Sciences Laboratory |publisher=[[Harvard University]] |access-date=October 3, 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241003182642/https://visionlab.harvard.edu/members.alumni.php?memberID=graduate |archive-date=October 3, 2024 |url-status=live |quote=Martin Wainwright, graduate student (PhD), 1994–1996}}</ref> In 2002, Wainwright completed his Ph.D. in electrical engineering and computer science at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) under the supervision of Alan S. Willsky and Tommi S. Jaakkola. His dissertation, which he developed at the [[MIT Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems]],<ref name="LIDS2022joins" /><ref name="LIDS2011data" /> was titled ''Stochastic processes on graphs with cycles: geometric and variational approaches''.<ref name="PhDthesis" /><ref name="mgp">{{mathgenealogy|id=128115|title=Martin James Wainwright}}. {{Retrieved|access-date=October 3, 2024}}</ref> For his thesis, Wainwright received the electrical engineering and computer science department's George M. Sprowls Award for the best Ph.D. thesis in computer science.<ref>{{cite magazine |date=June 4, 2003 |title=2003 MIT Award Winners – Electrical engineering and computer science |url=http://web.mit.edu/newsoffice/2003/print/awards-eecs-0604-print.html |magazine=[[MIT Tech Talk]] |publisher=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] |volume=47 |issue=31 |page=12 |hdl=1721.3/204350 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041124182924/http://web.mit.edu/newsoffice/2003/print/awards-eecs-0604-print.html |archive-date=November 24, 2004 |access-date=October 4, 2024 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Following his Ph.D., Wainwright moved to the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he was a postdoctoral researcher for [[Michael I. Jordan]] from 2002 to 2004.<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael I. Jordan (CV) |url=https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/jordan-cv.pdf |website=Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences at UC Berkeley |publisher=[[University of California, Berkeley]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160804165034/http://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~jordan/jordan-cv.pdf |archive-date=August 4, 2016 |quote=Postdoctoral Supervision ... Martin Wainwright, 2002–2004 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=EECS/ERL Roster (no students) |url=http://www.cs.berkeley.edu/Rosters/roster.name.nostudentee.html |website=Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences at UC Berkeley |publisher=[[University of California, Berkeley]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020811224205/http://www.cs.berkeley.edu/Rosters/roster.name.nostudentee.html |archive-date=August 11, 2002 |url-status=dead |quote=[Name:] Wainwright, Martin James ... [Status:] Postdoctorate ... [Sub-Affiliation:] jordan }}</ref> In the fall of 2004, he joined the faculty at the University of California, Berkeley with a joint appointment between the Department of Statistics and the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences.<ref>{{cite web |title=New Faculty in EECS |url=http://www.eecs.berkeley.edu/Faculty/Lists/new.shtml |website=Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences at UC Berkeley |publisher=[[University of California, Berkeley]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041024005153/http://www.eecs.berkeley.edu/Faculty/Lists/new.shtml |archive-date=October 24, 2004 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Martin Wainwright: Biography |url=http://www.eecs.berkeley.edu/~wainwrig/biography.html|website=Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences at UC Berkeley |publisher=[[University of California, Berkeley]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050401041426/http://www.eecs.berkeley.edu/~wainwrig/biography.html |archive-date=April 1, 2005 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Martin Wainwright |url=https://old.simons.berkeley.edu/people/martin-wainwright |website=[[Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing]] |date=26 April 2013 |access-date=October 4, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=EECS Faculty List |url=http://www.eecs.berkeley.edu/Faculty/Lists/list.shtml |website=Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences at UC Berkeley |publisher=[[University of California, Berkeley]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041009180345/http://www.eecs.berkeley.edu/Faculty/Lists/list.shtml |archive-date=October 9, 2004 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In July 2022, he returned to MIT, becoming the Cecil H. Green Professor in both the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, where he is in the Faculty of Artificial Intelligence and Decision-Making, and the Department of Mathematics.<ref>{{cite web |title=New Faculty (2021-2022) |url=https://computing.mit.edu/faculty/new-faculty-2021/ |website=[[MIT Schwarzman College of Computing]] |publisher=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |archive-date=July 29, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240729075748/https://computing.mit.edu/faculty/new-faculty-2021/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="LIDS2022joins" />

==Awards and recognition==
Wainwright has received multiple awards for his work, including the [[COPSS Presidents' Award]] from the [[Committee of Presidents of Statistical Societies]] in 2014 for his "fundamental and ground-breaking contributions to high-dimensional statistics, graphical modelling, machine learning, optimization and algorithms{{nbsp}}..., as well as new methodology with wide-ranging implications for numerous applications".<ref>{{cite web |title=COPSS Awards at JSM |url=https://imstat.org/2014/10/01/copss-awards-at-jsm2014/ |website=[[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |date=October 1, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2014 COPSS Presidents' Award Winner |url=https://community.amstat.org/copss/awards/presidents/2014 |website=[[Committee of Presidents of Statistical Societies]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |archive-date=May 30, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240530220219/https://community.amstat.org/copss/awards/presidents/2014 |url-status=live }}</ref> From the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], he received a Medallion Award and Lecture in 2013<ref>{{cite web |title=IMS Special Invited Lecturers in 2013 |url=https://imstat.org/2012/10/03/ims-special-invited-lecturers-in-2013/ |website=[[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |date=October 3, 2012 |archive-date=June 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230610145053/https://imstat.org/2012/10/03/ims-special-invited-lecturers-in-2013/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and the Blackwell Award and Lecture in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=Special Lectures in 2017 |url=https://imstat.org/2017/05/15/special-lectures-in-2017/ |website=[[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |date=May 15, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Honored Special Awards & Lecturers Recipient List |url=https://imstat.org/ims-special-lectures/honored-special-awards-lecturers-recipient-list/ |website=[[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] |access-date=October 4, 2024}}</ref>

He was awarded a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] in 2005,<ref>{{cite web |title=Sloan Research Fellowships – Research Fellowship Award Winners of 2005 |url=http://www.sloan.org/programs/fellowshiplist.shtml |website=[[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050404185023/http://www.sloan.org/programs/fellowshiplist.shtml |archive-date=April 4, 2005 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2005 Annual Report |url=https://sloan.org/storage/app/media/files/annual_reports/2005_annual_report.pdf |publisher=[[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |page=2 |archive-date=September 6, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240906001504/https://sloan.org/storage/app/media/files/annual_reports/2005_annual_report.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> [[National Science Foundation CAREER Award]] in 2006,<ref>{{cite web |title=CAREER: Novel Message-Passing Algorithms for Distributed Computation in Graphical Models: Theory and Applications in Signal Processing |url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=0545862 |website=[[National Science Foundation]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241004143921/https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=0545862 |archive-date=October 4, 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> and a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 2024.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Costello |first1=Sarah |title=Three from MIT awarded 2024 Guggenheim Fellowships |url=https://news.mit.edu/2024/guggenheim-fellowships-0426 |website=[[MIT News]] |publisher=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |date=April 26, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Fellows: Martin J. Wainwright |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/martin-j-wainwright/ |website=[[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |archive-date=July 23, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240723005450/https://www.gf.org/fellows/martin-j-wainwright/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Wainwright was selected as a [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics#Fellows|Fellow of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 2014 "for his fundamental research in statistical machine learning and high-dimensional statistics".<ref>{{cite web |title=IMS Fellows 2014 |url=https://imstat.org/2014/07/01/ims-fellows-2014/ |website=[[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |date=July 1, 2014 |archive-date=April 19, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419132325/https://imstat.org/2014/07/01/ims-fellows-2014/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Martin Wainwright is named IMS Fellow |url=https://statistics.berkeley.edu/about/news/prof-martin-wainwright-named-ims-fellow |website=Department of Statistics at UC Berkeley |publisher=[[University of California, Berkeley]] |access-date=October 4, 2024 |date=July 25, 2014}}</ref>

==Publications==
In addition to numerous peer-reviewed articles in journals and conference proceedings, Wainwright has (co-)authored the following three books:
* {{cite journal |last1=Wainwright |first1=Martin J. |author-mask1= |last2=Jordan |first2=Michael I. |author-link2=Michael I. Jordan |year=2008 |title=Graphical Models, Exponential Families, and Variational Inference |url=https://www.nowpublishers.com/article/Details/MAL-001 |url-status= |url-access=subscription |format= |type= |series= |volume=1 |issue=1–2 |journal=Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning |pages=1–305 |doi=10.1561/2200000001 |isbn=978-1-60198-184-4}} 
* {{cite book |last1=Hastie |first1=Trevor |author-link1=Trevor Hastie |last2=Tibshirani |first2=Robert |author-link2=Robert Tibshirani |last3=Wainwright |first3=Martin |author-mask3= |year=2015 |title=Statistical Learning with Sparsity: the Lasso and Generalizations |url= |url-status= |url-access= |format= |type= |series=Monographs on Statistics and Applied Probability |volume=143 |edition= |location=New York |publisher=Chapman and Hall/CRC |page= |pages= |doi=10.1201/b18401 |isbn=978-1-4987-1216-3}} 
* {{cite book |last1=Wainwright |first1=Martin J. |author-mask1= |year=2019 |title=High-Dimensional Statistics: A Non-Asymptotic Viewpoint |url= |url-status= |url-access= |format= |type= |series=Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics |volume=48 |edition= |publication-place= |location= |publisher=Cambridge University Press |page= |pages= |doi=10.1017/9781108627771 |isbn=978-1-108-49802-9}}
